Messages.Author: self biased
Messages.Body:
while teaching some new people how to play recently, i noticed there was a tendency to get confused as to what actions have stealth by default, especially with actions that say "+1 Stealth Action" they would try to use the '+1 stealth' as modifiers. Chalk it up to 'learning the game' but it did get me thinking about the way natural Stealth is displayed on the card. with "1 vote" being added to political cards in the green bar why can we not add "1 stealth" to actions that have the text "+1 stealth?" Indeed, we could also eliminate text from the rulebook describing that equipping and employing allies/retainers happens at +1 stealth, because it would be printed on the card that the action takes place at 1 stealth.

as an example, The Embrace as it is now:

and using the convention i've described cards would look like this:

that would leave just the inherrent actions like bleed, hunt, rescue, &c. to describe in the rulebook.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body: I find this too hard to read and too easy to miss for my taste. The goal is not bad, but I am not sure how to do it while keeping a good visibility.

However, the 1 vote happens only with a referendum, and a political card can only be pitched for a vote once per player per referendum. Stealth/Intercept happens WAAAAAAAY before it gets to that point. All you would need in the rulebook is a note that says something to the tune of "If an action occurs at stealth, it will say so below the action icon of the card."
>
I don't think that is relevant: people who have read and understood the rules already know the difference between an action and an action modifier. It is the others who need help.

One thing that could help would be to remove the + in action cards. Actions could be written with the default value, all other effects would have a + to indicate they change that default value.

Example for a Govern:

Govern the Unaligned

1
Bleed for 3.
1 stealth action. Move 3 blood from the bank to a younger vampire in your uncontrolled region.

Messages.Author: Pagan
Messages.Body:
Moving the +1 stealth text around doesn't seem to solve the problem.

A okayer who doesn't know the rules will see the +1 stealth up in the top left and make the same assumption as they would currently.

I've run into this problem teahcing a few players and explaining the rules solved the problem rather easily. It's such a minor thing that the work involved in updating all cards, and then having yet another card template in a deck (same card looks different than 2 other versions of the same card) or on the table to confuse players seems to outweigh the benefits.

I agree. It takes a game or two to distinguish actions from action modifiers, but I've found that it's a pretty easy lesson to learn if you emphasize the function of individual cards over the function of card types. Once you've played a stealth bleeder a few times, for instance, you start to realize that Govern lets you take an action, and Faceless Night lets you get that action through. When you pick up a new deck, you can then make an analogy: Shadow Play is sort of like Faceless Night, and Public Trust is sort of like Govern. At that point the action/action modifier distinction makes perfect sense.
